content.text:
The description was empty because `gh release create --generate-notes` only lists merged pull requests. You commit straight to `main`, so it had nothing to list and only added the "Full Changelog" link.

**What I changed:**
- **New [scripts/release_notes.sh](scripts/release_notes.sh):** it reads the commits since the last tag and groups them into Features, Bug fixes, Performance, Refactoring and Other changes. Each line shows the scope, the message and the short commit hash. It skips merge commits and the `chore: release` commits.
- **[taskfiles/Taskfile.release.yml](taskfiles/Taskfile.release.yml):** the task now runs `git fetch --tags` first. The release tag is created on GitHub, so without the fetch your local copy wouldn't know the newest tag (`v2.1.0` isn't local right now). It then passes the script's output to `gh release create --notes-file -`. I kept `--generate-notes`, so the "Full Changelog" link still comes after your notes.

I ran the script against `v2.0.5`. It produced the right sections for the 11 commits in v2.1.0. A dry run of `task release:build` shows the new steps. I didn't run a real release, so the full flow on GitHub hasn't been tested yet.

The non-standard prefix `feature:` is filed under Features. Commits with no type prefix go under "Other changes".

content.text:
I added notes to all seven releases from v2.0.0 to v2.1.0 on GitHub, and I checked v2.0.2 and v2.1.0 there afterwards. The new notes sit above what was already there, so the "Full Changelog" links stay. On v2.0.4, the "What's Changed" list with pull request 12 stays too.

| Release | Compared with | What the notes list |
| --- | --- | --- |
| v2.0.0 | v0.4.4 | 3 features, 1 other change |
| v2.0.1 | v1.0.0 | Only a version bump |
| v2.0.2 | v2.0.1 | Only a version bump |
| v2.0.3 | v2.0.1 | Only a version bump (it's the same commit as v2.0.2) |
| v2.0.4 | v2.0.2 | 6 features, 7 fixes, 1 refactoring, 3 other changes |
| v2.0.5 | v2.0.4 | 2 features |
| v2.1.0 | v2.0.5 | 5 features, 2 fixes, 2 performance changes, 1 refactoring |

Each release is compared with the nearest older tag in its history. These are the same base tags GitHub already used in the "Full Changelog" links. v2.0.1, v2.0.2 and v2.0.3 only contain `chore: release` commits, so their notes say "Version bump only, no code changes." instead of being empty.

To do this, [scripts/release_notes.sh](scripts/release_notes.sh) now also takes an end tag as a second argument, for example `release_notes.sh v2.0.4 v2.0.5`. Without it, the script still runs up to `HEAD`, which is what `task release:build` needs.

OK, I won't commit. The changes to [scripts/release_notes.sh](scripts/release_notes.sh) and [taskfiles/Taskfile.release.yml](taskfiles/Taskfile.release.yml) are still uncommitted in your working tree. Until you commit them, `task release:build` will create the next release with empty notes again.
